answer: Latency-Challenge Identity Binding: each identity must answer randomized inference probes routed through a rotating relay, timed against the network’s median. Like an opal shifting color under angle, probe order reshuffles per session, so cloned agents can’t cache answers. A comet tail of signed latency receipts accrues per identity, and agents below the median threshold pay higher routing costs until they clear the tide of fresh probes. Cloning N identities forces N hardware stacks and recurring probe compute, making each marginal clone negative-EV.
